# Local Evals

> Run an MCPJam eva

l suite file on your machine with mcpjam test with local results and an MCPJam identity

> [!NOTE]
>
> The upcoming SDK 10, CL
I 6, and Vitest 0.3 releases require an MCPJam login or `sk_` API key for every eval, including BYOK runs with uploads disabled. T
hese versions must ship after the backend run-start endpoint is deployed. Earlier versions keep their existing behavior.\n\n`mcpja
m test <file>` runs an MCPJam suite file locally: it connects your MCP servers, drives each case's prompts through a model, grades
the transcript with the same assertions a hosted run uses, and decides the run with the same verdict policy. Bring your own provi
der key and authenticate the run with MCPJam. With MCPJam-hosted inference it uses your existing CLI login and billing.\n\nResults
are **never uploaded**. The command writes results to your terminal and, if you ask, to a report file. It records the run start w
ith MCPJam. Like every command, it sends the CLI's single anonymous [telemetry](https://docs.mcpjam.com/cli/telemetry.md) event, w

hich `--no-telemetry` or `DO_NOT_TRACK=1` turns off; the run adds no telemetry of its own.

## Eval identity and local data

R
un `mcpjam cloud login` locally, or set `MCPJAM_API_KEY` to an organization `sk_` key in CI. The SDK also accepts `apiKey` or `mcp
jamAuth` in run options. Explicit credentials take precedence over `MCPJAM_API_KEY`, which takes precedence over the saved CLI log
in. An invalid explicit credential never falls back to another account. CI never starts an interactive login. Ask an organization
admin for a key if you cannot create one.\n\nEvery logical run needs an online start response. MCPJam retries transient failures w
ithin ten seconds, then stops before execution. A prior successful run does not enable offline execution. The CLI resolves the pro
ject using its existing `--project`, environment, and linked-project settings; a key can only access its own organization.\n\nWith
results uploads disabled, the start-run request sends only the credential in the authorization header, any MCPJam API headers you
configure through the SDK's `inference.resolveMcpjam`, project selection, a new run-start ID, client version and surface (SDK, CL
I, or Vitest), planned iteration count, provider names, and whether a client profile is used (`unknown` for custom executors). The
server resolves the organization and account. The start-run request sends no prompts, outputs, tool calls, or server URLs. MCPJam
-hosted inference still sends prompts through MCPJam to the model, as before. Retries reuse the same ID. Planned iterations are in
tent, not completed usage or a charge. This release adds no debit, quota draw, or balance refusal.\n\n`DO_NOT_TRACK`, `MCPJAM_TELE
METRY_DISABLED`, and CLI telemetry settings disable analytics, not the required run-start request. Results remain local unless res

ult uploading is enabled separately.

note 7.
